items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results. Authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings open. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of exploitation. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; permit only bounded reversible growth that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data-handling, claims, and platform boundaries. Continue existing read-only security evidence work using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Do not access credentials or private containers, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix. Record dated, redacted evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Do not create duplicate requests or production work.
